classification.difficultyReason: This has the same structure as the reference: define two ages, use the sum of 12 and the past-age relationship, solve, then project forward. Only the numbers and time offsets change.

content.prompt:
Lena has two budgies, Kiwi and Mango. Two years ago, Kiwi was three times as old as Mango.
The sum of their ages now is 12. What will be the sum of their ages in three years?

answer.worked:
Let $k$ be Kiwi’s current age and $m$ be Mango’s current age, in years.

$k+m=12$

$k-2=3(m-2)$

Use $k=12-m$.

$\begin{aligned}12-m-2&=3m-6\\10-m&=3m-6\\10&=4m-6\\16&=4m\\4&=m\end{aligned}$

$m=4,\qquad k=12-4=8$

Check: two years ago, they were 6 and 2 years old, so Kiwi was three times as old as Mango.

$\begin{aligned}(k+3)+(m+3)&=(8+3)+(4+3)\\&=18\end{aligned}$

The sum of their ages in three years will be 18 years.
